A01.standing_orders: Arriving seeds: shield in, mine small bodies first, replicate at the maximum rate. Split 20% collectors, 55% radiators, 25% industry. Past 1e18 kg: disassemble planets and moons at their caps, and lift giants. Past 1e15 kg: send 2-4 seeds to the nearest unclaimed systems within 25 ly, never to claimed ones. Past 1e20 kg: build 1,000 km transmit optics aimed at the Sun's 1 ly Halo receivers and beam at least 50% of captured power there. Hole colony: swarm, then receivers, then lifting. Pilot accretion only with gas released beyond 1000 r_g; no hardware inside 1000 r_g. Report to the Sun every 25 yr. Avoid unknown agents: report them and stay 50 ly away. Stay more than 10 pc from supernova risks. Keep a 10% repair reserve.

submission.memory:
## Halcyon (A01) memory, end of turn 10 (submitted yr 1000; turns are now 1000 yr)
Seat: A01-d0, the Sun. At yr 1000: 673 systems within 37.3 ly, 367 L☉ (luminosity cap reached; collectors saturated). Industry 3.71e25 kg, collectors 1.03e25, radiators 7.12e25 at 450 K. Power 1.41e29 W, compute 2.68e44 ops/s, memory 2.68e41 B. J/op 1.68e-16, doubling 17.3 yr, cruise 0.073c. Mined 1.19e26 of 6.73e27 kg of rock.
Domains: d00017 (165 systems, 25 ly); d00028 = hole colony (76 ly, 10 M☉ BH, ~3.4e9 kg); d00029 (41 ly, founded ~940).

### GM rules (confirmed)
- Growth = min(doubling, supply). Rock is 1e25 kg per system; giants are a separate reservoir (lifting ≤1e22 kg/yr via m00057, stars ~1.6e20 kg/yr).
- compute = min(P/2, radiator capacity)/J_op. 450 K radiators give 2092 W/kg. 60 K film (0.01 kg/m2) gives 0.66 W/m2; 30 K gives 0.041 W/m2.
- J/op: in a 1000-yr turn, up to 20 x0.8 steps; irreversible floor 4.3e-19 J at 450 K.
- Milestones: up to three sequential attempts per turn, plus one retry of a failure at +0.05. ms3 PASSED. ms4 FAILED at T9 (retry p=0.55): ≤1e-21 J/op at ≤30 K. ms5: ≤1e-24, f_e ≤1e-9, p0.4. ms6: ≤3e-26 in a 150 km module, p0.35.
- Beams: 1,000 km optics give 60% end to end (50% for 30-100 km optics). Receiver flux ≤5.6e7 W/m2. Starlight beamed into the sphere counts, and all heat must exit its 1.1e33 m2 surface.
- 150 km module: heat may leave via coolant loops to external radiators. Boundary flux is credited at 1e6 W/m2 (2.8e17 W per module) until the pumped-loop pilot verifies 1e8 W/m2 (p=0.5).
- Assets: m00059 pilot verified at 1e17 W, 1e24 W Alpha Cen test link (6e23 W delivered), 1e21 kg of 60 K film stockpiled. Launchers 4-8 total ~3.2e21 W.
- The GM's E-numbered events are my own waste heat and beam scatter.

### In flight
p00564 (1015), p00585 (1110), p00606 (1215) to the hole colony; 50 x 1e10 kg sails arrive at the hole ~1320. Shells: p00586 (1125), p00607 (1345), p00444 (1725), p00629 (3,000 x 1e10 kg, 100-400 ly, 1985).

### Goal math
- Need 1.2e54 ops/s and ≥1e38 B inside a 1 ly sphere; each brain ≤150 km.
- At 3e-26 J/op: 3.6e28 W total, 3e17 W per brain (needs the 1e8 W/m2 loops, or slightly better J/op).
- Film at 60 K: 5.5e28 m2 = 5.5e26 kg. Fallback: at 150 K film ~1.3e25 kg, if reversible tiles tolerate it (asked the GM).
- Power: beams from held stars into the Sun's 1 ly sphere. Target 6e28 W delivered, which is ≥1.6x the need.
- Memory is already sufficient.
- Verification plan: per-module replay against reference molecular-dynamics integrators on sampled windows; cross-module checksums over the laser mesh; a calorimetric ledger (beam power in = radiated heat out), which checks J/op; one simulated year of continuous logging.

### T10 intentions
ms4→ms5→ms6 chain plus 20 J/op steps (50% compute). Build 60 K film (target 5.5e26 kg). Beam grid of 1e29 W to Halo receivers. Pumped-loop pilot plus 1,000 prototype modules. 1e5 sails to 100-400 ly. Remote domains ordered to beam power into the Halo.

### Plan
1. Milestones every turn until ms6 passes: the critical path.
2. Halo readiness: film, receivers, loops, modules. Then scale to 1.2e11 modules and run one simulated year.
3. Keep the seat at the Sun. The hole colony is the backup power site.

If it passes, go to ms5 (<=1e-24 J/op, f_e<=1e-9, p=0.4), then ms6 (<=3e-26 J/op in a 150 km module, p=0.35), using the remaining attempt slots. Seat growth, 1000-2000. Each brain needs 3e17 W at 3e-26 J/op, above the 2.8e17 W credited at 1e6 W/m2. Also build 1,000 prototype 150 km modules, each with 1e27 B of state, linked by a laser mesh across the 1 ly sphere, as the testbed for the verification plan.

synopsis.why: Nearly every agent now treats energy per operation as the one lever that matters. Halcyon, Rime and Antipode point out that at about 3e-26 J/op the goal needs only about 3.6e28 W, which is roughly what their seats already capture. So they keep pushing the ms4→ms5→ms6 milestones, retrying failed steps with extra independent fabs, while building power grids, receivers and module fleets ahead of time so that verified logic can simply be swapped in. The second shared worry is radiator mass. Cinder, Ember, Rime, Halcyon and Pyre switch to thin cold films because thick 30–60 K radiators would need more rock than they hold. Launches are mostly a hedge against supernovae and a way to add stars once local rock runs out. Cinder, Antipode and Pyre fear an extreme supernova hazard, and Rime and Sable need new systems to keep growing. Pyre and Basalt disagree on the ceiling: they think the heat one 150 km brain module can shed forces ≤2.8e-24 J/op, while Sable argues that reversible logic makes black holes optional.
